question: During the streamer's trips to Shanghai and Chengdu, which of the following ingredients did the streamer eat while having hot pot? 1. Fat beef rolls; 2. Shrimp paste; 3. Duck tongue; 4. Luncheon meat?

rollouts.answer: 2. shrimp paste, 3. duck tongue, 4. luncheon meat (says beef rolls NOT eaten)

db_evidence.notes: episodes:30sec text around 232354-232384 ('discovering it's beef, inviting rudy to try it') and 232714-232744 ('discovers a duck tongue') give strong textual support for items 1 and 3 in Chengdu, and are retrievable by a plain time-windowed run_sql over the Chengdu total_interval -- rollouts 1 and 3 (and partially 4) recovered item 1 only when their clip_qa window happened to start before 232397 and include the 232354 episode; rollout 0 and 2's narrower/absent Chengdu windows missed it. Critically, episodes:30sec:007756 (232534-232564) explicitly states the streamer 'notes that both are beef and that he's allergic to shrimp', and the broader show repeatedly establishes a running shellfish-allergy bit (rows 175368, 189197-189797). This directly explains why the reference answer excludes item 2 (shrimp paste). This row was returned by rollout 0's own run_sql call (which spanned both Shanghai and Chengdu windows) but was buried in a ~57KB dump and never acted on; no rollout's semantic_search or run_sql was ever specifically targeted at 'allergy'/'shrimp' text, and no rollout reconciled the clip_qa 'eats shrimp paste' visual call against this textual evidence. All five clip_qa calls that examined the Shanghai orange-piece item independently converged on labeling it 'shrimp paste' being eaten, suggesting either a genuinely ambiguous visual (an orange/pink processed item that looks like shrimp paste) or a systematic visual-agent bias toward that label from the question's own ingredient list priming it.

root_causes: Wrong/inconsistent Chengdu clip_qa time windows: item 1 (fat beef rolls) is only recoverable if the visual sub-agent's window starts before ~232397s to catch the 232354-232384 beef-discovery episode; rollouts 0 and 2 used windows that excluded this moment and both concluded (or partly concluded) beef rolls were not eaten.

Systematic visual misidentification of item 2 (shrimp paste): all 5 rollouts' clip_qa calls independently identify an orange/pink piece in the Shanghai footage as 'shrimp paste' being eaten, contradicting the reference answer and the DB's explicit text that the streamer is allergic to shrimp and avoids it.

Retrieved-but-unused text evidence: the shellfish-allergy line (episodes:30sec:007756) was pulled into context by at least one rollout's run_sql call but never surfaced in reasoning or cross-checked against the clip_qa 'shrimp paste eaten' claim -- no rollout ran a targeted semantic_search/run_sql for allergy or shellfish context specifically.
One rollout (4) exhibits a location-misattribution error, moving Shanghai-only beef-platter evidence into a Chengdu answer clause despite its own Chengdu clip_qa explicitly denying beef rolls there.

Rollout 0 asserts a Chengdu duck-tongue finding in its final answer without ever having called clip_qa on the Chengdu interval, indicating unverified/hallucinated corroboration layered on top of a single Shanghai-only visual check.
what_worked: Rollouts 1 and 3 used clip_qa windows starting before the Chengdu clue interval's nominal start and thereby correctly recovered fat beef rolls (item 1) and duck tongue (item 3).
All rollouts correctly identified luncheon meat and duck tongue as eaten, matching the reference on 2 of 3 'yes' items via direct clip_qa visual confirmation.
The judge's partial-credit scoring (2-3 out of 5) reasonably reflects that every rollout got roughly 2-3 of the 4 items right rather than being wildly off.
transferable_lessons: For multi-location 'which of these did X eat' questions, run clip_qa windows that start a bit before the given total_interval start, since the specific discovery/eating moment for an item can occur just before the labeled clue window.

When a visual sub-agent identifies an ambiguous food item by appearance alone (e.g. an orange/pink piece labeled 'shrimp paste'), cross-check it against any textual/dialogue evidence in the memory DB (e.g. allergy statements, explicit ingredient naming) rather than trusting the visual call alone -- a specific run_sql/semantic_search for allergy or ingredient-naming keywords across the whole trip would have caught the shellfish-allergy line.

Do not carry a finding from one location's clip_qa call (e.g. Shanghai beef-platter arrival) into the final answer's claim about a different location (Chengdu) -- attribute each visual finding strictly to the window it came from.

Do not state a location-specific visual finding (e.g. 'Chengdu footage shows X') in the final answer unless a clip_qa call was actually made on that location's interval; otherwise it is an unverified inference.
open_questions: Why did the judge score rollout 0 (score 3) higher than rollout 2 (score 2) for nearly textually identical wrong answers ('2,3,4 eaten, beef rolls not eaten') -- likely judge scoring noise rather than a substantive difference.

Whether the orange/pink item eaten in Shanghai is genuinely ambiguous between shrimp paste and another processed item (e.g. a fish/pork paste ball) was not resolved by directly inspecting a frame in this analysis; all conclusions about item 2 rely on the DB's allergy text plus the reference answer, not on independently viewing the Shanghai frames.
